body.heading: Sunlight is a mixture
paragraphs: Sunlight looks white, but it is really all the colours of the rainbow mixed together. You can see the mix when light splits into a rainbow.
The air around Earth is full of tiny bits too small to see. When sunlight bumps into them, the blue part of the light gets scattered — bounced around — more than the other colours.

body.heading: Blue everywhere
paragraphs: The scattered blue light bounces all over the sky, so wherever you look in the daytime, blue light reaches your eyes. That is why the whole sky looks blue.
Try it indoors: your adult shines a torch through a glass of water with a tiny drop of milk in it. From the side, the water can look faintly blue.

body.heading: Sunset colours
paragraphs: At sunset, sunlight travels a much longer way through the air. By the time it reaches you, most of the blue has bounced away, leaving reds and oranges.
So the same scattering that makes the sky blue at lunch paints it orange at bedtime.

takeaway: The sky is blue because air scatters blue sunlight everywhere, and sunsets lose the blue on the long journey.
materials: A drop of milk (an adult helps)
safetyNotes: An adult should hold the torch and the glass. Never shine a torch into anyone's eyes, and never look at the Sun.
screenFreeExtension: Watch the sunset colours with your adult and name every colour you can spot.
